newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kas-Associatie sees growth through euro.
newsitem.headline: Kas-Associatie sees growth through euro.

text.p: Kas-Associatie NV, the bank for the Dutch equity trade, said it expected the upcoming common European currency would offer good prospects of international expansion for the company.

"The introduction of the euro will expand our natural market areas and therefore our organic growth prospects," chairman Sandor von Balluseck told a news conference on Kas-Associatie's 1996 annual report.
He said Kas-Associatie would offer its services to international banks and brokers, for which it could handle back-office activities for European securities.

Clearing and custody in their home markets would always be done by these banks themselves but contracting out these services to a party which could do them in other countries has become increasingly popular.
"Instead of having six custodian banks in just as many countries, such a client would only have to keep one," Von Balluseck said.

Kas-Associatie expects a common currency would make it "less foreign" for non-Dutch clients. It would also meet more foreign competitors in its markets but Kas-Associatie's high financial ratings gave it a competitive edge, Von Balluseck said.
Kas-Associatie expects to haul in most of this new international business through its London office, but most of the back-office activities will be handled in Amsterdam.
The company will gear up its organisation to be able to technically handle the expected international expansion.
"It will not be an easy task but we think this should be technically possible within 12 to 18 months and we also expect it to be interesting from a commercial point of view," Von Balluseck said.
Kas-Associatie earlier reported it expected the 1997 first half net profit to grow substantially from the year-ago period.
Favourable market trends had continued in the first three months of this year and clients' activities had remained high.

"Although the first few weeks of April showed a more quiet picture, we expect our 1997 first half profit to grow considerably from the 12.9 million guilders of the first half of 1996," Von Balluseck said. He added he could not yet give a full-year forecast.

In 1996, the company's full-year net profit surged by 65 percent to 24.1 million guilders. Kas-Associatie said this rise had not only been caused by favourable trends in financial markets but also because it had increased all its market shares.
